title: unify tenant-scoped init templates and sane hook timeouts for private helm charts
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Helm: unified tenant-scoped init templating, configurable hook timeouts/backoff, idempotent init-job leader lock, and improved preflight checks for VPC deployments.
description:
Context and motivation: Private deployments run into edge cases during upgrades and initial installs when tenant initialization jobs run concurrently across namespaces or when cloud preflight validations (VPC CIDR overlap, required subnets) are flaky. We've had incidents where init jobs retried indefinitely due to short hook timeouts and where rollback hooks failed because templating was duplicated across charts. This PR consolidates init-hook templates, introduces tenant-scoped helpers, and makes hook timeouts/backoff explicit in values to avoid brittle defaults.

Summary of changes (single PR):
- Move all tenant/init-related hook templates under charts/_helpers.tpl as 'redwood.tenantInit.*' helpers and reference them from private and core subcharts to avoid duplication.
- Add a leader-election based idempotent init job pattern: the init job now uses a ConfigMap lock (configurable name) so only one init run per-tenant proceeds at a time. This avoids races when multiple cluster-ops processes try to initialize the same tenant.
- Expose hook lifecycle parameters in values.yaml: preflight.timeoutSeconds (default 300), preflight.backoffLimit (default 4), init.hookGracePeriod (default 60), rollback.hookTimeout (default 180).
- Add templated annotations that surface the associated Terraform module version and workspace (annotations.terraform.redwood.com/module and .workspace) to improve correlation during upgrades.
- Implement a tiny preflight Job helper that validates: cluster k8s version range, required CRD presence, and optional VPC CIDR overlap check when vpc.enabled=true. The VPC check is opt-in and guarded by values.preflight.vpcCheck: true.
- Update chart tests (helm-unittest harness) to cover the new helper templates and to assert that hooks are marked as Helm hooks with proper weights for init -> post-install ordering.
- Add an upgrade note in README/UPGRADE.md describing the leader-lock behavior and recommended values for high-concurrency installs.

Files changed (high-level):
- charts/_helpers.tpl (new helpers for tenant init and hook annotations)
- charts/private/templates/init-job.yaml (refactored to use helpers and leader-lock)
- charts/private/values.yaml (new keys under preflight, init, rollback, annotations.terraform)
- charts/private/templates/preflight-job.yaml (new opt-in preflight job)
- charts/private/templates/rollback-hook.yaml (refactored for explicit timeouts and safe retries)
- tests/helm/unittest/* (updated and new unit tests)
- docs/UPGRADE.md (upgrade notes)

Commit summary:
- a1c3f9d: add tenant init helper templates and hook annotation helpers
- 5b8d2a4: implement leader-lock pattern for init job
- e4f7b2c: expose hook timeouts and backoff in values.yaml with defaults

Review conversation highlights: 
- Maya Patel (reviewer): "Nice consolidation — helpers reduce duplication a lot. One request: make the leader lock ConfigMap name configurable and include namespace fallback logic so the lock can live in a central 'control' ns for air-gapped installs."
- Author (Avery): "Agree. Added values.init.lockConfig.mapName and values.init.lockConfig.namespace with sensible defaults (chart namespace). Also included a short note in UPGRADE.md advising operators to set the namespace to their central control namespace if they run cross-tenant controllers."
- Luis Ortega: "Preflight VPC check is helpful. Could we ensure it respects network policies and does not require cluster-admin? Suggest falling back to a lightweight pod-based probe where possible."
- Author: "Implemented a conservative probe that validates via 'kubectl get' of the relevant NetworkAttachment or cloud-provider CIDR annotation when available; documented permissions needed. Kept the vpcCheck opt-in to avoid unexpected RBAC demands."
- Samir Kaur: "We should ensure rollback hooks have exponential backoff to avoid hot loops on repeated failures during partial upgrades."
- Author: "Added backoffLimit and used helm hook weights to separate init, install, and rollback flows. Documented the default backoffLimit=4 and how to tune it."

CI and rollout:
- CI pipeline (unit tests + helm lint + integration smoke) initially failed on a flaky test (helm-unittest assert on hook weight). Fixed by adjusting test harness and adding an explicit weight in helper.
- Final CI status: pass across linux/amd64 runners. Integration smoke job passed against a kube 1.24 cluster in our test pool.

Migration and operational notes: 
- No breaking API changes to values.yaml; new keys are additive. However, operators relying on the previous implicit behavior where multiple init jobs could race may observe reduced parallelism due to the leader-lock. If you relied on parallel initialization to speed up massive multi-tenant rollouts, set values.init.parallelism to control workers or temporarily disable the lock (not recommended).
- For VPC-enabled installs, enable values.preflight.vpcCheck=true in CI for each environment to detect CIDR overlap early. The check is conservative and may require read access to cloud annotations.

Related tickets and context: ENG-4762 (tenant init races on large upgrades), ENG-4810 (preflight validations for VPC installs), SUP-1982 (customer reported rollback failures during Private v1.8 -> v1.9 upgrade).

Merge strategy: squash and merge. The PR was squash-merged to keep the history focused on the logical change.

Testing checklist (kept in PR body):

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add an operator-mode alternative to the init job that can be run as a long-lived controller for very large fleets (ENG-4901).
- Add e2e tests covering preflight VPC checks against simulated cloud metadata (ENG-4920).

If any reviewer wants to revert a specific helper or wants the lock implementation to be different for on-prem vs cloud, happy to split this into a smaller follow-up — kept the PR scope focused to templating + timeouts + preflight so ops can adopt quickly.
